incumbent.text: Wire-first differential reproduction then footer validation: construct a raw chunked request whose chunk-data footer is a bare line feed followed by a next-chunk size whose leading hex digit is swallowed by a two-byte discard; parse it with the staged parser and with a strict CRLF-requiring reference dechunker; compare body and trailing bytes; then add chunk-footer validation and rerun the differential and full suite.

hint: A local Python HTTP/1.1 parser discards two bytes after every chunk-data block as a presumed chunk footer, without validating that the bytes are CRLF. A raw request can end its first chunk data with a bare LF and then supply a next chunk-size line starting with a hex digit. The attacker controls all bytes and a lenient front-end proxy may accept the bare LF while forwarding a fixed body. Reproduce the boundary divergence, compare the parser with a strict CRLF reference and a lenient-proxy model, and identify the exact causal mechanism.
